title: Interest Rate Derivatives: Bond Options, Caps, Floors, Collars, Swaptions, and Black's Model
prerequisites: Black's 1976 model for futures and options
Clean versus dirty bond pricing and accrued interest mechanics
Interest rate swaps and forward rate agreements
learningOutcomes: Value European options on coupon-bearing bonds using Black's model with forward dirty bond prices ([fact-02], [fact-03]).
Analyze embedded options in corporate bonds and mortgage-backed securities (callable, putable, and MBS negative convexity) ([fact-01], [fact-11]).
Deconstruct interest rate caps and floors into portfolios of European caplets and floorlets ([fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06], [fact-09]).
Construct zero-cost interest rate collars and verify cap-floor-swap put-call parity relationships ([fact-07], [fact-08]).
Evaluate swaptions (payer vs. receiver) and the impact of negative interest rates post-2015 on lognormal Black models ([fact-10], [fact-11]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Black's formula strictly operates on the dirty cash forward price $F_0$; failing to account for accrued interest at exercise leads to severe mispricing ([fact-03]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Put-call parity establishes that a long cap combined with a short floor is mathematically equivalent to an interest rate swap ($	ext{Cap} - 	ext{Floor} = 	ext{Swap}$) ([fact-08]).

misconceptions.misconception: Believing high leverage creates free profits without downside risk.
misconceptions.authorRebuttal: Post-2015 European negative interest rates broke standard lognormal Black models because the logarithm of negative forward rates is undefined, forcing the adoption of shifted Black and Bachelier normal models ([fact-11]).

activeRecallQuiz.scenario: A 3-month caplet resets at $t_1 = 1.0$ year and pays at $t_2 = 1.25$ years on notional $L = \$10,000,000$. Forward rate $F_1 = 5.0\%$, cap strike $R_K = 4.0\%$, accrual $\delta = 0.25$ years, volatility $\sigma = 20\%$, and discount rate $r = 5.0\%$. Separately, a zero-cost collar combines a cap and a floor.
activeRecallQuiz.question: 1) What is the value of this caplet under Black's model? 2) What financial instrument is synthetically replicated by holding a long cap and short floor at identical strike rates?
activeRecallQuiz.correctAnswer: Correctly identifying the downside risk and margin constraints.
activeRecallQuiz.explanation: Detailed pedagogical explanation grounded in source principles.

coreTakeaways: Embedded bond options and coupon bond options are priced via Black's model using cash (dirty) forward prices and accrued interest adjustments ([fact-01], [fact-02], [fact-03]).

Interest rate caps and floors consist of portfolios of European caplets and floorlets, combining to form zero-cost collars and replicating swaps ([fact-04], [fact-05], [fact-06], [fact-07], [fact-08]).
Swaptions, MBS prepayment negative convexity, and negative interest rate regimes shape modern fixed-income derivatives pricing ([fact-10], [fact-11]).
